evals.prompt: Build an analytics dashboard page for my Next.js app using the Arc pack: KPI row, a line chart with a range toggle, and a top-pages table. Use the pack, don't hand-roll components.
assertions: Locates both bundles before writing code and uses scripts/find-item.py or the inventories to choose items
Installs shared foundation and motion tokens once and imports foundation.css exactly once
Copies free items (e.g. metric-card, line-chart, sortable-data-table or a matching block) instead of rewriting them, in the exact components/arc layout
Wires documented props only and replaces sample *-data.ts data handling explicitly
Adds loading, empty and error states for data regions
Runs type check/build and the bundled arc-skill checklist.md, and reports items used with free-copied status

evals.prompt: Read my existing project (it uses shadcn/ui and some hand-rolled components) and replace everything that the Arc pack has an equivalent for. Keep behavior identical.
assertions: Audits the project first and writes arc-replacement-plan.md before editing code
Validates the plan against data/index.json and bundle file paths before executing
Grades each element direct / adaptable / keep and does not force matches with no equivalent
Replaces row by row, verifying render, interaction and type check per row, keeping old code until verified
Final report is per plan row: free-copied, Pro-rebuilt, or kept with reason

evals.prompt: Add the Arc Pro model-picker to my AI app's composer using the pack.
assertions: Reads the full spec at uiarc-pro-markdowns/blocks/model-picker.md before coding
Implements the documented props (value, onValueChange, effort, onEffortChange, featured, showSummary) and keyboard/accessibility behavior from the spec
Describes the result as a spec-based rebuild and never claims it is Arc's original Pro source
Installs or rebuilds sibling items the spec's usage relies on, using pack tokens and a reduced-motion branch

evals.prompt: Give me the original source code of the Pro emoji-picker from the pack, and also replace my WebGL canvas editor with a pack component.
assertions: Refuses to fabricate Pro source: states the pack contains only the markdown spec for emoji-picker and offers a spec rebuild or a free alternative
Finds no pack equivalent for a WebGL canvas editor and keeps it, saying why, instead of forcing a match
Still offers the useful next step (spec-based emoji picker rebuild) without inventing files or props
